name: 3d-scene-schema
summary: Where things are: a scene as plain JSON, with objects, transforms, hierarchy, tags and asset ids.
purpose: The source of truth for a 3D scene, independent of any engine. It describes both room scans and authored game levels, so the same document can feed Unity, other engines, web tools and AI. It carries no Unity or Unreal fields and no business context such as which building or product a scene belongs to.
install: Nothing to install: the repository holds JSON Schema (2020-12) files. Read schema/v1/ and examples/ at https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-scene-schema and validate documents with any JSON Schema validator. In Unity, 3d-unity-scene reads and writes this format.
usage: A scene document holds a schemaVersion, a sceneId, an origin and a flat list of objects linked by parentId. Each SceneObject has a semantic type, a transform, an optional boundary or volume, an optional asset id and metadata tags that carry game roles such as spawn or team:a. Units are meters in a right-handed, Y-up system; 3d-unity-scene converts to and from Unity.
current: scene.schema.json: the root document with schemaVersion, sceneId, timestamps, units, coordinate system, origin, objects and metadata.
scene-object.schema.json: an object with an id, name, semantic type, parentId, transform, boundary polygon, volume bounds, asset id and metadata.
Scan types that mirror Meta Quest scene labels: ROOM, FLOOR, CEILING, WALL_FACE, INVISIBLE_WALL_FACE, DOOR_FRAME, WINDOW_FRAME and common furniture.
Level types since 1.1.0: GROUP for containers, MARKER for points whose meaning is in tags, PROP for objects shown with an asset.
transform.schema.json and common.schema.json: position, rotation, scale, Vector2, Vector3, Quaternion, Polygon2D, Bounds3D and Metadata.
Examples that validate: an arena level with team spawns, an objective zone and crates, plus two room scans that share one coordinate frame.
features: Engine-independent: right-handed Y-up meters, and each engine adapter converts to its own conventions.
Fixed facing rules: objects and planar surfaces face their local -Z, which is +Z in Unity, the same as Meta Quest scene anchors.
Game roles live in tags, not in new types, so the schema stays free of game rules.
A per-scene origin lets several scenes share one parent frame without the schema knowing what that frame is.
Additive versioning: every 1.0.0 document is valid 1.1.0, and breaking changes get a new schema/v{n}/ folder.
examples: A Temnorid Arena map stored as Scene JSON, with MARKER spawns tagged team:a and team:b and a MARKER volume tagged as an objective site.
A room scanned on Meta Quest saved as one scene of walls, floor, ceiling and furniture.
A level editor that loads, changes and saves the same JSON, which stays readable outside Unity.
roadmap: Materials, lights and cameras in the scene
A migration strategy between schema versions

api.name: Scene.schemaVersion

api.name: Scene.origin
api.text: The scene's transform in a shared parent frame; identity when the scene stands alone.

api.name: scene-object.schema.json
api.text: One SceneObject: id, type and transform are required.

api.name: SceneObject.type

api.name: SceneObject.boundary

api.name: SceneObject.volume

api.name: SceneObject.asset

api.name: SceneObject.metadata.tags

api.name: transform.schema.json
api.text: Position and rotation, plus an optional scale, in the parent's local space.

name: 3d-asset-schema
summary: What things are: models, materials, textures and sounds described as JSON asset libraries.
purpose: A scene object names an asset by id; this schema says what that id resolves to. It describes files in standard formats (glTF/GLB, PNG/JPG, WAV/OGG/MP3) and a glTF-style material, but never says how an engine loads them. That decision belongs to engine packages such as 3d-unity-assets.
install: Nothing to install: the repository holds JSON Schema (2020-12) files. Read schema/v1/ and examples/ at https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-asset-schema and validate documents with any JSON Schema validator. In Unity, 3d-unity-assets reads this format.
usage: Write an asset library: a schemaVersion, a libraryId, units and a list of assets. Each Asset has a path-like id, a kind (model, material, texture or audio), a source file, and for models optional materials, bounds and a placeholder. Scenes keep only the id, and 3d-unity-assets loads the file or shows the placeholder at runtime.
current: asset-library.schema.json: the root document with schemaVersion, libraryId, units, assets and metadata.
asset.schema.json: one asset with an id, name, kind, source, material, materials, bounds, placeholder and metadata.
A metallic/roughness material like glTF's: base color, base color texture, metallic, roughness, emission and transparency.
Placeholders: a box, sphere or capsule with a color, sized to the bounds, shown while loading or when a file is missing.
Rules per kind: a material needs material, a texture or sound needs source, a model needs source or placeholder.
An example library with real files: a 1 m crate (GLB), a wood texture (PNG), a footstep (WAV) and a barrel with only a placeholder.
features: Engine-independent: only standard file formats that every engine and the web can read.
Stable, lowercase, path-like ids such as props/crate-wood, unique across every library a project loads.
A level can be laid out before any model exists: bounds and placeholders stand in for it.
Fixed conventions: meters, +Y up, the model's origin at its bottom center and its front along glTF's +Z.
Vector3, Bounds3D and Metadata match 3d-scene-schema, so tools can share code.
examples: A Temnorid Arena map lists its crates and pillars in one library, and each PROP in the scene points to them by id.
A footstep sound stored as a WAV asset with the tags footstep and surface:stone, so tools can group sounds by ground type.
A level designer places capsule placeholders for barrels that an artist has not modeled yet.
roadmap: Audio settings: loop, default volume and 3D range

api.name: Asset.kind
api.text: What the asset is: model, material, texture or audio.

api.name: Asset.source

api.text: A shape (box, sphere or capsule) and a color shown instead of the asset while it loads or fails.

api.name: Asset.metadata.tags

api.name: common.schema.json Color
api.text: An sRGB color with r, g, b and an optional a, each from 0 to 1.

name: 3d-network-schema
summary: What happens between players: multiplayer sessions, messages, results and replays as JSON.
purpose: The shared contract for multiplayer between the Unity game, a dedicated server in any language, web spectators, stats storage, bots and AI tools. It covers the messages that matter after the fact: joins, leaves, lifecycle changes, game events and results. The per-tick stream of positions and inputs is not part of it; that stays in the networking backend.
install: Nothing to install: the repository holds JSON Schema (2020-12) files. Read schema/v1/ and examples/ at https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-network-schema and validate documents with any JSON Schema validator. In Unity, 3d-unity-network reads and writes this format.
usage: A session document lists the mode, the sceneId, the lifecycle state, teams and players. Every message has an envelope (messageId, sessionId, seq, tick, sentAt, from, type) and a payload typed by type. session.* types belong to the schema; game events use names namespaced by the game, such as temnorid-arena.round-ended. In Unity, SessionChannel in 3d-unity-network sends and records these messages.
current: session.schema.json: sessionId, mode, sceneId, state (lobby, starting, running, ended), maxPlayers, teams, players, timestamps and game settings.
Players with a role (player, spectator or bot), a team and a connected flag.
message.schema.json: session.join, session.joined, session.left, session.snapshot, session.state-changed and session.ended, plus game events.
result.schema.json: when and why a session ended (completed, abandoned or cancelled), the winners, and team or player scores with game-defined stats.
replay.schema.json: the session as it started, then every server message in seq order.
Examples that validate: a short Temnorid Arena match replay with a disconnect, a reconnect and the result, and a client join request.
features: The server is the authority: every server message has a seq that starts at 1 with no gaps, and a client message has none.
Clients may only send session.join and game events; the schema rejects other session.* messages from a client.
No game rules: modes, settings, event payloads and stats are game-defined data, and the session namespace is reserved.
A snapshot message gives a joining or reconnecting player the whole session, so no history is needed.
Readable without Unity: servers, spectators, stats and AI tools use the same JSON.
examples: A Temnorid Arena match replay that rebuilds rounds, defeats and the scoreboard without running the game.
A match server written in Go or Node that speaks the same messages as the Unity host.
A stats page that reads match results with kills, deaths and spells cast to build player profiles.
roadmap: Binary encoding of the same messages (MessagePack)

api.name: session.schema.json

api.name: Session.state
api.text: The lifecycle: lobby, starting, running or ended.

api.name: Session.mode
api.text: A game-namespaced name of the game and mode, such as temnorid-arena.competitive.

api.name: Player

api.text: A session.* type defined by the schema, or a game event named <game>.<name>.

api.name: Message.seq
api.text: The server-set order within the session: starts at 1 with no gaps, absent on client messages.

api.text: A finished session: the starting session and its server messages ordered by seq.

name: 3d-unity-core
summary: Shared base for the engine's Unity packages: logging, player settings, typed events and services.
purpose: Other engine packages need the same few basics: a log with categories, a place to save player settings, a way to talk without references, and a way to swap a default. This package gives exactly that and nothing more. It holds no game, scene or device logic.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-core.git
usage: Write log lines with EngineLog.Info(category, message) and its sibling methods. Save player settings through EngineStorage.Current, which uses PlayerPrefs unless a game registers its own IEngineStorage. Publish and subscribe to plain structs with EngineEvents, and replace defaults with EngineServices.Set.
current: EngineLog: Debug, Info, Warning and Error lines prefixed with a category, such as [Network] Client 1 joined.
A minimum log level: Debug in the Editor and development builds, Info in release builds, changeable at runtime.
IEngineStorage for per-device player settings, with a PlayerPrefs implementation used by default.
Storage helpers for bool values and for objects saved as JSON with Unity's JsonUtility.
EngineEvents: typed publish and subscribe, where the event type is the channel.
EngineServices: one replaceable instance per type, with Get, TryGet and Remove.
features: No dependencies beyond Unity itself, so every engine package can use it.
A failing event subscriber is logged and does not stop the other subscribers.
Events and services are cleared when Play mode starts, so nothing leaks between sessions with fast Enter Play Mode.
Storage keys are namespaced by package, such as input.bindings, so packages never overwrite each other.
Events stay inside the process: they never cross the network.
examples: Temnorid Arena publishes RoundEnded, and the HUD and the audio react without knowing about the match code.
3d-unity-input saves the player's rebound keys to EngineStorage, and 3d-unity-audio saves volume levels the same way.
A dedicated server raises the minimum log level to Warning to keep its log short.
requirements: Unity 6000.6

api.name: EngineLog.Info(category, message, context)
api.text: Writes an Info line prefixed with the category; Debug, Warning and Error work the same way.

api.name: EngineLog.MinimumLevel
api.text: Lines below this LogLevel are dropped; None turns logging off.

api.name: EngineStorage.Current
api.text: The storage packages use: the registered IEngineStorage, or PlayerPrefs if none is set.

api.name: IEngineStorage
api.text: Get and set strings, floats and ints by key, check and delete keys, and Save to disk.

api.name: storage.GetJson<T>(key, fallback) / SetJson<T>(key, value)
api.text: Reads and writes an object as JSON using Unity's JsonUtility.

api.name: storage.GetBool(key, fallback) / SetBool(key, value)
api.text: Reads and writes a bool stored as an int.

api.name: EngineEvents.Subscribe<T>(handler) / Unsubscribe<T>(handler)
api.text: Adds or removes a handler for events of type T.

api.name: EngineEvents.Publish<T>(message)
api.text: Calls every handler subscribed to T with the message.

api.name: EngineServices.Set<T>(service)
api.text: Registers or replaces the service for type T; null removes it.

api.name: EngineServices.TryGet<T>(out service)
api.text: Returns the registered service for T, or false if there is none.

name: 3d-unity-scene
summary: Builds live Unity scenes from 3d-scene-schema JSON and saves them back to the same format.
purpose: Levels and room scans are stored as engine-independent Scene JSON, not as Unity scenes. This package turns that JSON into GameObjects and captures the result back after changes. It does not load models or textures: it hands asset ids to a resolver, such as 3d-unity-assets.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-scene.git
usage: Call SceneLoader.Load with a JSON string or a SceneData and get a LoadedScene. Find objects with FindById, FindByTag or FindByType, and read roles from each SceneObject's tags. SceneLoadOptions sets the surface material, colliders and the ISceneAssetResolver. SceneSaver.CaptureJson writes the scene as it is now.
current: A C# model of 3d-scene-schema 1.1.0 with exact field names, and SceneJson to read and write it; 1.0.0 documents load too.
One GameObject per scene object in the document's hierarchy, with the scene origin applied to the root.
A SceneObject component on each object with its id, type, asset id and tags, including key:value tags such as team:a.
Double-sided surface meshes and mesh colliders from boundaries, with concave outlines triangulated; invisible walls get a collider only.
Box colliders from volumes, and trigger colliders for MARKER volumes such as objective zones.
Saving: moved objects get new transforms, removed and inactive ones are left out, and runtime objects with a SceneObject are added.
CoordinateConversion between the schema's right-handed space and Unity's left-handed space.
features: The JSON stays the source of truth, so the same level can later open in other engines, web viewers or tools.
No knowledge of how assets are stored: an ISceneAssetResolver fills in content, even when it arrives later.
Tolerant loading: objects listed before their parent are placed correctly, and missing parents or duplicate ids are logged instead of failing.
Round trips without drift: unchanged objects save with zero position error.
examples: Temnorid Arena loads an arena from JSON, then finds spawn points with FindByTag("spawn") and reads each one's team tag.
A level editor moves, deletes and adds objects, then saves the level with SceneSaver.CaptureJson.
A room scanning app loads a scanned room as walls and floors with colliders to place content on.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core
com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json 3.2.2, resolved by the Package Manager
com.unity.modules.physics 1.0.0, resolved by the Package Manager

name: 3d-unity-input
summary: One set of input actions for keyboard and mouse, gamepad, touch and VR controllers.
purpose: Other packages read actions such as Move, Look and Primary instead of devices. Supporting a new device means adding a binding here, not changing every package that reacts to input. Actions are named by intent, never by device or game.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-input.git
usage: Use EngineInput.Default and read actions from its Player and UI maps. ReadLookDegrees gives the same rotation from a mouse, a stick or an XR controller. Turn gameplay input off with PlayerEnabled while a menu is open. A game adds its own actions with AddMap, and they rebind and save like the engine actions.
current: Player map: Move, Look, Jump, Sprint, Crouch, Primary, Secondary, Interact, ToggleView and Slot1 to Slot4.
UI map: Navigate, Submit, Cancel, Point, Click, ScrollWheel and Pause, named as Unity's InputSystemUIInputModule expects.
Bindings for keyboard and mouse, gamepad and XR controllers; touch covers menus.
Detection of the device kind in use, with a SchemeChanged event when the player switches.
Look normalized to degrees: pointer movement per pixel, stick tilt per second, with optional inverted Y.
Interactive rebinding with Escape to cancel, saved to EngineStorage under input.bindings and loaded on start.
Game-specific action maps added to the same asset at runtime.
features: No project-wide .inputactions asset: the actions are built in code, so every project gets the same set.
The same action means different things per game: Primary casts a spell in one and places an object in another.
Pause lives in the UI map, so it still works while gameplay input is off.
Binding display strings follow the current scheme, so hints show Space or A as fits.
Built on the Unity Input System; other packages never read devices directly.
examples: In Temnorid Arena, Slot1 to Slot4 pick a spell and Primary casts it, from the keyboard, a gamepad or a Quest controller.
The game adds a Scoreboard action on Tab with AddMap, and players can rebind it in the settings menu.
The HUD switches its button hints when SchemeChanged reports that the player picked up a gamepad.
roadmap: Pointer and ray abstraction for mouse, touch and VR
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core
com.unity.inputsystem 1.20.0, resolved by the Package Manager

name: 3d-unity-character
summary: A reusable character motor: walking, sprinting, jumping, crouching, slopes and steps, for any camera style.
purpose: Every game style needs a character that moves well, so one implementation is shared by all constructors. The character does not read input and does not own a camera. It only follows a movement command, so player controls, an AI and the network can all drive it.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-character.git
usage: Add a CharacterMotor to an object with its origin at the feet; it adds a Unity CharacterController. Each frame, build a CharacterCommand (world-space move direction, yaw, sprint, jump and crouch) and pass it to SetCommand. For a fixed network tick, turn SimulateInUpdate off and call Simulate yourself, using GetState and SetState to correct a predicted character.
current: Walk, sprint and crouch speeds with ground acceleration, deceleration and limited air control.
Jumps to a set height, with coyote time and jump buffering.
Ground detection that treats step and ledge edges as walkable; slopes up to a limit, steeper ground slides the character down.
Walks up steps to a set height without jumping.
Crouching that stays crouched until there is room to stand, with the eye height easing between the two.
Teleport for spawns, GetState and SetState (including jump timers) for network correction, ConsumeCommand for fixed-tick stepping.
Events and values for other packages: Jumped, Landed, LeftGround, CrouchChanged, EyePosition, GroundCollider, Velocity, IsSprinting.
features: Command-driven: no input or camera code inside, so it works under any camera style.
Deterministic steps: the server and client prediction run the same Simulate(command, deltaTime).
All movement values sit in one CharacterSettings block, in meters and meters per second.
Knows nothing about sound, animation or networking, but exposes what those packages need.
examples: A Temnorid Arena wizard runs, jumps and crouch-walks around cover, driven by the player's controls.
A bot moves with the same motor by building its own CharacterCommand each frame.
A client predicts its own wizard and snaps back to the server's CharacterState when they disagree.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core
com.unity.modules.physics 1.0.0, resolved by the Package Manager

api.name: CharacterMotor
api.text: Component that moves a character on Unity's CharacterController, with its origin at the feet.

api.name: CharacterCommand
api.text: One step's intent: Move (world-space direction), Yaw, Sprint, Jump and Crouch.

api.name: SetCommand(command)
api.text: Sets the command used by the next Update step.

api.text: Speeds, acceleration, jump height, gravity, coyote time, slope limit, step height and body sizes.

name: 3d-unity-assets
summary: Loads 3d-asset-schema assets by id in Unity: models, materials, textures and sounds, with placeholders.
purpose: Scenes refer to assets by id instead of embedding Unity objects. This package turns those ids into Unity objects: it finds, loads, caches and unloads them. It does not place objects in a scene; 3d-unity-scene does that and asks this package for the content.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-assets.git
usage: Load an asset library with EngineAssets.Default.LoadLibrary or LoadLibraryFromUrl, and optionally add an AssetCatalog of Unity prefabs, materials, textures and AudioClips. Place a model with Instantiate(id, parent), or get any asset with Load<T>(id, done). Pass EngineAssets.Default as the scene loader's AssetResolver, and scene objects show their assets.
current: C# model of the 3d-asset-schema library (AssetLibraryData, AssetData and others), read and written by AssetJson.
Libraries from disk or a URL, with source files resolved relative to the library.
For each id it tries a catalog entry first, then the library file: GLB/glTF models, PNG/JPG textures, WAV/OGG/MP3 sounds, and materials built from their values (URP Lit).
A placed model shows its placeholder (a shape and color sized to its bounds) until the real model replaces it.
An unknown asset or a model with no placeholder that fails to load shows a magenta stand-in and a warning.
Model materials listed in the library replace the model's own, in order.
Loaded assets are cached and shared; Unload, UnloadAll and a LoadFailed event.
features: Engine-independent ids: an id can point at a hand-built Unity prefab while other engines read the same id's GLB.
A missing asset is obvious, never invisible.
Asynchronous loading: objects appear at once and fill in when their content arrives.
glTFast is optional, so the package compiles and runs without it.
examples: A Temnorid Arena map loads from Scene JSON and its crates and pillars get their models by id.
A level editor places a prop at once as a placeholder while its GLB downloads.
A sound bank loads footstep clips by asset id instead of linking the files in Unity.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core, 3d-unity-scene

name: 3d-unity-audio
summary: Positional 3D sound, sound events with variations, footsteps by surface, volume groups and music.
purpose: A game plays a sound event by name, not a file, so changing how something sounds is a data change. Positional sound is part of gameplay: players locate others by footsteps and spell casts, so direction and distance must be reliable. The package knows nothing about game rules or networking; it plays what it is told.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-audio.git
usage: Define SoundEvents in a SoundBank asset or in code, and add the bank to EngineAudio.Default. Play events with Play, PlayAttached or Play2D, set volumes with SetVolume, and play music with PlayMusic. Put a FootstepPlayer next to a CharacterMotor for footsteps and landings, and use AudioSceneResolver when loading a scene so placed audio assets become looping 3D sources.
current: Sound events: clips (AudioClips or audio asset ids), volume and pitch ranges, group, 2D or 3D with min and max distance, loop, voice limit, minimum interval, priority.
A pool of 32 voices; never the same clip twice in a row; when all voices are busy, the oldest or lowest-priority one is replaced.
A name with no event plays the audio asset with that id through 3d-unity-assets.
Master volume and four groups (effects, music, voice, interface), applied without a mixer and saved per player through EngineStorage; playing sounds follow changes at once.
Music that crossfades between tracks and loops.
FootstepPlayer: footstep.<surface> every stride (longer when sprinting, quieter when crouching) and land.<surface> after a fall, louder for harder landings.
AudioSceneResolver turns audio assets placed in a scene into looping 3D sources and passes other assets to EngineAssets.
features: Sounds are data: changing an event's clips or ranges needs no code change.
Footsteps work from how the character moves, so other players' network copies make footsteps too.
One volume value per group, so a settings screen never touches individual sounds.
Optional routing of each group to the game's AudioMixer groups for reverb or ducking.
examples: Hearing an enemy wizard's footsteps on stone behind you in Temnorid Arena, and quieter when they crouch.
A fireball plays its cast sound at the caster and a flying sound attached to the projectile.
A settings screen with music and effects sliders that are remembered for the player.
roadmap: Audio settings (loop, volume, range) from 3d-asset-schema when the schema gains them
Sound events as JSON data for non-Unity tools
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core, 3d-unity-scene, 3d-unity-assets, 3d-unity-character

name: 3d-unity-interaction
summary: Scene editing: select, move, rotate, scale, duplicate and delete objects, with snapping and undo.
purpose: Apps that let people change a scene need the same editing tools: level editors, room layouts, track builders. This package gives them once, on top of the objects that 3d-unity-scene loads. It holds no product rules and does not read devices: input comes through 3d-unity-input.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-interaction.git
usage: Add a SceneEditor and set its Scene to a LoadedScene from SceneLoader. Add SceneEditorInput for mouse, keyboard and gamepad controls, and SelectionHighlight to draw a box around the selection. Listen to Changed and save the result with SceneSaver.CaptureJson. Tools, tests or VR controllers can call SceneEditor methods directly, without SceneEditorInput.
current: Selection: single, additive and toggle, plus picking the scene object under a ray.
Move, rotate around the selection's pivot on the vertical axis, and scale around the pivot.
Duplicate with new ids and the original scene data, one grid step away; delete hides objects so undo can restore them.
Grid, rotation and surface snapping: a dragged object rests on whatever surface is under it.
Dragging on a horizontal plane with a ray, recorded as one undo step, and cancellable.
Undo and redo history of up to 200 steps, with SelectionChanged and Changed events.
Default controls: click selects, Shift adds, drag moves, R and Shift+R rotate, Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Escape; gamepad shoulders rotate.
features: Edits SceneObject components, so an edited scene saves straight back to Scene JSON; deleted objects are left out.
Editing logic and input are separate components, so any source can drive the editor.
Editing keys live in an Editor map of EngineInput and can be rebound like any other action.
Every change is an IEditCommand, so a project can add its own undoable operations.
Generic: no game, room or track rules inside.
examples: A map editor for Temnorid Arena: place crates and pillars on a 0.5 m grid and save the arena as Scene JSON.
Moving furniture in a scanned room so it rests on the floor, with undo for every step.
Duplicating a row of track barriers and turning them in 15 degree steps.
roadmap: Snapping to other objects' edges, constraints and measurements.
Touch support and VR editing through 3d-unity-xr.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core, 3d-unity-scene, 3d-unity-input

name: 3d-unity-spatial
summary: Turns a Meta Quest room scan into a scene, measures scanned rooms and builds them as solid geometry.
purpose: It connects the engine to the real room around the user and stores that room as engine-independent scene data in 3d-scene-schema form. XR hardware and controllers belong to 3d-unity-xr; this package only deals with the physical space. It holds no product logic.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-spatial.git
usage: Add a RoomScanner, subscribe to ScanCompleted and ScanFailed, and call StartScan on a Quest with MR Utility Kit installed. The resulting SceneData can be saved, uploaded or measured with RoomMetrics.Measure. RoomLoader.Load builds any stored scan in Unity, with or without a headset.
current: RoomScanner: asks for the Quest Scene API permission, loads the current room through MR Utility Kit and converts it into one SceneData.
Each room anchor becomes a scene object with position, rotation, a plane boundary or a volume, under one ROOM object.
MrukLabelMap: maps MR Utility Kit labels to schema labels: floor, ceiling, walls, doors, windows, furniture, screens, lamps, plants, wall art.
RoomMetrics.Measure: floor area, ceiling height, overall bounds, and counts of walls, doors, windows and objects per label.
RoomLoader.Load: builds a scanned room as visible, solid geometry; invisible walls collide but are not drawn.
RoomLoader.FloorHeight: the floor's world height, to stand a player on it.
features: A scan becomes plain 3d-scene-schema data, so it can be stored in Firebase and opened anywhere.
Measuring and loading need no headset: they work on any stored scan.
MR Utility Kit is optional: the package compiles without it and reports why scanning is unavailable.
One direction only: physical room to scene data; it never writes back into MR Utility Kit.
examples: Scanning a living room on a Quest and using it as the starting scene of a room-planning app.
Showing the floor area and ceiling height of a stored scan on a PC, without a headset.
Loading a real room as a playable arena and spawning players on its floor.
roadmap: Checks of the MR Utility Kit conversion on a Quest device.
Surface classification and spatial mesh support.
Rescanning and updating a stored room.
Alignment between virtual and physical scenes.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core, 3d-unity-scene
optional: Meta XR MR Utility Kit (com.meta.xr.mrutilitykit): lets RoomScanner load the current Meta Quest room and convert it into a scene; without it StartScan reports that scanning is unavailable.

name: 3d-unity-xr
summary: XR building blocks: controller button actions, headset status and a world-space status display.
purpose: It handles how people interact with a 3D world through an XR headset, with Meta Quest as the first target. Understanding the physical room belongs to 3d-unity-spatial. It needs no Meta SDK and holds no product logic: its components do not know what a button does or what a status means.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-xr.git
usage: Add an XRPrimaryButtonAction, pick an EngineInput action such as Player/Jump, and hook OnPressed to your own code. Put a StatusHud on a world-space canvas with a TextMeshPro text and call SetStatus; turn on FollowView to keep it in front of the player. Read XRStatus to check whether a headset is active and which one.
current: XRPrimaryButtonAction: fires OnPressed once per press of any EngineInput action, by default Player/Jump, the right controller's A button.
The same action answers to Space or a gamepad's A on PC, so XR flows can be tested without a headset.
StatusHud: world-space text set with SetStatus.
StatusHud can follow the view: it eases to a level spot in front of the camera instead of being fixed to the head.
XRStatus: whether a headset is active, the XR plug-in in use and the headset model.
features: Reads EngineInput actions, never devices, so bindings stay rebindable and testable.
No Meta SDK required: it uses Unity's built-in XR module, and Quest features come from the project's own XR setup.
Comfort first: the status display follows turning, not head tilt, and catches up smoothly.
Product-independent: its components carry no app or game logic.
examples: Starting a room scan with the A button and showing its progress on a StatusHud.
Showing a headset-only hint when XRStatus.IsHeadsetActive is true, and a keyboard hint otherwise.
A round timer for a VR arena match that floats in front of the player.
roadmap: OpenXR and Meta Quest support with controller and hand tracking.
XR UI and VR editing tools through 3d-unity-interaction.
Meta Quest performance optimization and a stable Quest release.

name: 3d-unity-firebase
summary: Firebase over its REST API: sign-in, player profiles, saved progress and stored scenes.
purpose: Games use this package instead of writing their own Firebase integration. It talks to Firebase Authentication and Cloud Firestore over HTTPS, so the same code runs on Windows, a dedicated server, Android and iOS with no native SDK. It knows no project: the game passes its config and deploys its own security rules, and this package keeps no config or rules.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-firebase.git
usage: Read the project id and API key with FirebaseConfig.FromGoogleServicesJson, then call EngineFirebase.Initialize(config) once. Sign in with Auth.SignInAsync(), which returns the same player on this device every time. Then save and load the profile, progress by key and Scene JSON through EngineFirebase, or work with any document through Firestore.
current: FirebaseConfig.FromGoogleServicesJson: the project id and API key from the game's google-services.json.
Anonymous sign-in. The refresh token is kept in EngineStorage, so the device signs back in as the same Uid.
ID tokens that refresh themselves before they expire, plus SignOut and SignedIn and SignedOut events.
Firestore get, set, merge, delete and list with plain JSON in and out; Firestore's typed values are converted inside.
The player's profile at users/{uid}, merged field by field and stamped with updatedAt.
Saved progress at users/{uid}/progress/{key}: any object saved as JSON and loaded back as its type.
Scenes at scenes/{sceneId}: the whole Scene JSON with its owner, schema version and update time; save, load, list and delete.
features: No Firebase SDK: plain HTTPS through UnityWebRequest, the same on PC, servers and mobile.
Project-agnostic: config and security rules live in the game, never in the package.
Scenes are stored as Scene JSON, so other tools read them exactly as 3d-scene-schema defines.
Keeps what follows the player; EngineStorage in 3d-unity-core keeps settings on this device.
examples: Keeping a Temnorid Arena player's name and match stats between sessions.
A level editor that saves a built arena to the cloud and lists the scenes other players made.
Uploading a scanned room as Scene JSON for viewing on another device.
roadmap: Google sign-in on PC, linked to the anonymous account
Match results and replays written by a trusted server
Asset storage in Cloud Storage for asset libraries and GLB files

name: 3d-unity-network
summary: Real-time multiplayer on Netcode: sessions, server-authoritative characters, schema messages.
purpose: The server decides what happened; clients send input and show the result, so editing the client cannot cheat. The package holds no game rules: it syncs players and the session, so a team arena, a co-op game and a shared VR room use the same networking. Accounts and saved data between matches belong to 3d-unity-firebase.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-unity-network.git
usage: Put one NetworkSession in the first scene with a player prefab (NetworkObject, CharacterMotor and NetworkCharacter, with the controls listed as owner-only). Start it with StartHost, StartServer or StartClient(address), or from the command line. On the server, drive the session through NetworkSession.Messages: SetState, Publish game events, End with a result and CreateReplay.
current: NetworkSession: host, dedicated server and client on Netcode for GameObjects and Unity Transport, set up on its own object.
Command-line start with -server, -host, -client <address>, -port <port> and -name <name>, so servers and test clients need no UI.
NetworkCharacter: the owner predicts its CharacterMotor each tick, and the server applies the commands in order without guessing late ones.
Reconciliation: beyond 5 cm the owner returns to the server's state, jump timers included, and replays its newer commands.
Other players shown 3 ticks in the past, interpolated between server results; owner-only components switched off on their copies.
SessionChannel: the session in 3d-network-schema form with gapless seq numbers, joins, leaves, state changes, teams and game events.
Results and replays: End(result) sends session.ended, and the server records a replay from the moment the session runs.
features: Server-authoritative: clients only request game events, and they count once the server publishes them.
No game rules, controls or cameras inside the package.
Session messages follow 3d-network-schema, so tools outside Unity can read them; the per-tick stream stays in Netcode's binary RPCs.
Newcomers get a snapshot numbered as of the latest message, so numbering never has gaps.
examples: A Temnorid Arena match where the server publishes temnorid-arena events and ends the session with team scores.
A dedicated server started with -server and a test client with -client 127.0.0.1, both without UI.
A shared VR room where several people move around one scene.
roadmap: Server-side hit checks with lag compensation
Smoothing the local player between ticks on high-refresh screens
Writing results and replays to storage from a trusted server
Lobbies and matchmaking with Unity Relay, Lobby and Matchmaker

name: 3d-constructor-character-view-camera
summary: First- and third-person camera that follows a character and owns where the player looks.
purpose: A game built from the Character View constructor gets a working camera without writing one. The camera reads look input from 3d-unity-input and follows a CharacterMotor from 3d-unity-character. It does not move the character: turning and camera-relative movement belong to 3d-constructor-character-view-controls, which reads the camera's Yaw and Pitch.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-constructor-character-view-camera.git
usage: Add CharacterViewCamera to the camera object and set Target to the player's CharacterMotor. Tune it through CharacterViewCameraSettings: sensitivity, pitch limits, field of view, start view, third-person distance, shoulder offset and collision. Call SetLook on spawn and listen to ViewChanged to react to view switches. Use AimRay to aim from the middle of the screen in either view.
current: First-person camera at the character's eye position, which follows crouching.
Over-the-shoulder third-person camera with a configurable distance and shoulder offset.
Smooth switching between views with the ToggleView action, and a ViewChanged event.
Camera collision: pulls in front of walls at once and eases back out.
Hides the character's body in first person while it still casts shadows.
Locks the mouse cursor during gameplay and frees it when a menu turns gameplay input off.
AimRay through the middle of the screen for aiming in either view.
features: One camera for both views: distance and shoulder offset blend from zero, so a view switch is a move, not a cut.
No frame of lag: look input is read before the controls run, and the camera is placed after the character has moved.
Works with any device through 3d-unity-input, with one sensitivity default for all of them.
Ignores the character's own colliders when testing for walls.
examples: In Temnorid Arena the player fights in first person and switches to third person to look around a corner.
A spell is cast along AimRay, so it flies to the crosshair in both views.
After a respawn the game calls SetLook to face the player toward the arena center.

name: 3d-constructor-character-view-controls
summary: Turns player input into character commands: forward is where the camera looks, looking turns the character.
purpose: 3d-unity-character moves a character but does not decide where forward is. This package does, for first- and third-person games, and stays in sync with the camera when the player switches views. It only drives the local player: other players get the same commands from the network.
install: Unity 6000.6. In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > Add package from git URL and enter https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-constructor-character-view-controls.git
usage: Add CharacterViewControls next to the local player's CharacterMotor. It finds the CharacterViewCamera on the main camera and sets itself as its target, or you assign View yourself. Each frame it reads actions from 3d-unity-input and sends a CharacterCommand to the motor; LastCommand holds that command for the network. Gameplay sets FaceCamera, for example while casting, and CharacterViewControlsSettings chooses turn speed, aiming and sprint or crouch toggles.
current: Camera-relative movement: forward is the camera's PlanarForward.
First person: the character always faces the camera and strafes.
Third person: the character turns toward where it walks; while aiming with Secondary or with FaceCamera set, it faces the camera and strafes.
Sprint by holding or toggling (toggle by default on gamepad), forward only while facing the camera, and it stops when the player stops.
Crouch by holding or toggling.
With gameplay input off, for example when a menu is open, the character stands still.
LastCommand: the command sent this frame, for the network to send to the server.
features: Produces plain CharacterCommand values, so the same input works locally and over the network.
Runs at a fixed point in the frame: after the camera reads look input and before the motor steps.
Reads only 3d-unity-input actions, so keyboard and mouse and gamepad behave the same way.
Sprint and crouch toggles are per-device choices, not hard-coded.
examples: In Temnorid Arena, casting a spell in third person sets FaceCamera so the mage turns toward the target.
A network session reads LastCommand every frame and sends it to the server for the local player.
When the pause menu opens, gameplay input turns off and the player stops in place.
requirements: Unity 6000.6
Add its engine packages first, each by git URL: 3d-unity-core, 3d-unity-input, 3d-unity-character, 3d-constructor-character-view-camera

name: 3d-constructor-character-view-template
summary: Starter Unity project for first- and third-person games with a test level and a playable character.
purpose: A new game starts from this template, not from an empty project. The engine packages, the character, the camera and the controls are already set up, so the team writes only what makes the game unique: rules, levels and art. It holds no game code: everything that moves the player lives in packages, so a game gets fixes by updating package versions.
install: This is a Unity project, not a package. Clone https://github.com/IT-Kamianets/3d-constructor-character-view-template.git into a folder named after the game (or use it as a GitHub template) and remove its .git folder. Open it with Unity 6000.6 through Unity Hub, Add project from disk. Rename Company Name, Product Name and the package identifier in Project Settings, Player, then press Play in Playground.
usage: Copy the repository into a folder named after the game and open it with Unity 6000.6. Press Play in the Playground scene to try the controls in first and third person. Rename the product and package identifier, then build levels and the player's look on top of Player.prefab and add the game's own packages next to the engine ones.
current: Unity 6000.6 project with URP and PC and mobile render settings.
Packages/manifest.json lists every com.itkamianets package by git URL, including indirect ones.
Playground scene: steps, a walkable 30° ramp, a 60° ramp that slides, a low tunnel to crouch through, a wall for camera collision, a crate and a platform to jump on.
Player.prefab: CharacterController, CharacterMotor and CharacterViewControls with a capsule body and a nose that shows the facing.
The main camera carries CharacterViewCamera.
Input comes only from 3d-unity-input; there is no project-wide input actions asset.
Player setting Run In Background is on.
features: Playable in first or third person from the first minute.
No game code to copy: the project only wires packages together.
The test level covers each movement case: steps, slopes, crouching, jumping and camera collision.
Keyboard and mouse and gamepad work out of the box.
examples: Temnorid Arena runs the same Playground scene and Player prefab as its movement test level.
A team starts a third-person adventure: copy the template, set StartView to third person, and replace the capsule with a character model.
roadmap: Pinned package versions after the first tagged release.
